_README: PRODUCTION RETRIEVAL QUERIES — transcribed from session_triage, never synthesised.
227 distinct (host, alert_rule) shapes drawn from 3,199 real incidents TG has triaged.

TRANSCRIBED 2026-08-01. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-07: production now asks 353 distinct non-empty (host, alert_rule) shapes over 3,333 incidents, so this set covers 227/353 = 64% of them. The 2026-08-01 population was 229 shapes / 3,171 incidents, which is what the 227 below transcribe. This is a SNAPSHOT and it ages: a retrieval number computed here describes the queries production asked up to 2026-08-01, not the ones it asks now. Re-transcribe before quoting it as current, and say which date the number came from.
WHY NOT eval/corpus.json: its sites are all 'dc1' where the retrieval corpus uses 'nl'/'gr'
(intersection EMPTY) and 14 of its 16 hosts do not exist in the corpus. Labelling on it would
measure a scorer with weightSite structurally dead and weightHost dead for 88% of queries.
must_retrieve_any_of IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY ON EVERY ROW. Relevance is a human judgement and this
file does not fabricate one. An LLM-invented gold label would make every later hit@k number a
measurement of the labeller, not of the retriever. These labels are the one part of the retrieval
instrument that needs an operator, and leaving them empty is the honest state, not an oversight.
adversarial_near_misses IS NOT a judgement — it is DATA. It lists the corpus rows tied at the k=3
cut score, i.e. the rows the scorer cannot tell apart and currently separates by alphabetical
ExternalRef order. near_miss_total is the untruncated count; the list is capped at 12.
COVERAGE GAP, stated rather than hidden: only 45 of these 227 shapes (17% of incident volume) are
resolvable against the SHIPPED seed corpus, because production also loads a maintained corpus that
